question: The various shapes of the bright part of the moon as seen during a month are called as what? (RRB JE CE (19/09/2019) Shift 1 CBT 2)
options: Sizes of the moon
Shapes of the moon
Phases of the moon
Patterns of the moon
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Phases of the moon

Explanation:
The phases of the moon are the different forms of the illuminated part of the moon as seen from Earth. These phases change due to the moon's orbit around Earth. When the moon is between the sun and Earth, it is a new moon, and when it is opposite the sun, it is a full moon. Other phases include first quarter and last quarter. The lunar cycle completes in about 29.5 days, known as a lunar month.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What are moon phases? → Different appearances of the moon's illuminated part
☛ What is the duration of a lunar month? → About 29.5 days
☛ When does a new moon occur? → When the moon is between Earth and the sun
☛ When does a full moon occur? → When Earth, sun, and moon are aligned with Earth in the middle
☛ Difference between first and last quarter? → First quarter shows right half illuminated; last quarter shows left half
question_hi: एक माह के दौरान चंद्रमा के चमकीले भाग की दिखाई देने वाली विभिन्न आकृतियों को क्या कहा जाता है? (RRB JE CE (19/09/2019) Shift 1 CBT 2)
options_hi: चंद्रमा का आकार
चंद्रमा की आकृतियाँ
चन्द्रमा की कलाएँ
चंद्रमा के पैटर्न
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है चन्द्रमा की कलाएँ

Explanation:
चंद्रमा की कलाएँ पृथ्वी से दिखने वाले चंद्रमा के प्रकाशित भाग के विभिन्न रूप हैं। ये कलाएँ चंद्रमा की पृथ्वी के चारों ओर परिक्रमा के कारण बदलती हैं। जब चंद्रमा सूर्य और पृथ्वी के बीच होता है, तो अमावस्या होती है, और जब पृथ्वी के विपरीत दिशा में होता है, तो पूर्णिमा होती है। अन्य कलाओं में प्रथम चतुर्थी और अंतिम चतुर्थी शामिल हैं। चंद्रमा की कलाएँ लगभग 29.5 दिनों के चक्र में पूरी होती हैं, जिसे चंद्र मास कहते हैं।

question: Which of the following dams is located on the river Ravi? (RRB JE CE (19/09/2019) Shift 1 CBT 2)
options: Ukai
Baglihar
Pong
Thein
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Thein

Explanation:
The Thein dam, also known as Ranjit Sagar Dam, is located on the Ravi River in the state of Punjab, India. The dam was primarily constructed for hydroelectric power generation and irrigation purposes. It has been a significant point of dispute between Punjab and Jammu & Kashmir over water sharing. Among the other options, Ukai Dam is on the Tapti River in Gujarat, Baglihar Dam is on the Chenab River in Jammu & Kashmir, and Pong Dam is on the Beas River in Himachal Pradesh.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Alternate name of Thein Dam → Ranjit Sagar Dam
☛ Origin of Ravi River → Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh
☛ Tributaries of Ravi River → Budhal and Siwa
☛ Length of Ravi River → Approximately 725 km
☛ Dams on Ravi River → Ranjit Sagar (Thein) and Shahpur Kandi
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा बांध रावी नदी पर स्थित है? (RRB JE CE (19/09/2019) Shift 1 CBT 2)

question: Which hill station is located in Andhra Pradesh? (RRB JE CE (19/09/2019) Shift 1 CBT 2)
options: Dalhousie
Horsley Hills
Darjeeling
Nainital
solution:

question: Which of the following is an endemic species in India? (RRB JE CE (19/09/2019) Shift 1 CBT 2)

Panda

question: Odisha shares its border with ________ Indian states.  (RRB JE EE (19/09/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: Four
Six
Five
Three
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Four

Explanation:
Odisha is a state located in eastern India, sharing its land border with four Indian states. These states are West Bengal (northeast), Jharkhand (north), Chhattisgarh (west), and Andhra Pradesh (south). To its east lies the Bay of Bengal, forming a maritime boundary. Thus, Odisha's land border touches only four states, not five or six. This fact is crucial for geography general knowledge in competitive exams.

☛ Which state lies to the west of Odisha? → Chhattisgarh
☛ Which state lies to the south of Odisha? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Which state lies to the northeast of Odisha? → West Bengal
question_hi: ओडिशा की सीमा ________ भारतीय राज्यों के साथ लगती है। (RRB JE EE (19/09/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options_hi: चार
छह
पांच
तीन
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है चार

Explanation:
ओडिशा पूर्वी भारत में स्थित एक राज्य है, जिसकी सीमा चार भारतीय राज्यों से लगती है। ये राज्य हैं: पश्चिम बंगाल (उत्तर-पूर्व), झारखंड (उत्तर), छत्तीसगढ़ (पश्चिम), और आंध्र प्रदेश (दक्षिण)। ओडिशा के पूर्व में बंगाल की खाड़ी है, जो समुद्री सीमा बनाती है। इस प्रकार, ओडिशा की भूमि सीमा केवल चार राज्यों के साथ जुड़ती है, न कि पांच या छह। यह जानकारी भूगोल के सामान्य ज्ञान में महत्वपूर्ण है।

question: A group of stars, which has a recognisable shape is called as (RRB JE EE (19/09/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: Comet
Constellation
Meteorite
Meteoroid
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Constellation

Explanation:
A group of stars that forms a recognizable pattern in the sky is called a constellation. Constellations are imaginary outlines drawn by connecting stars, such as Ursa Major or Orion. The International Astronomical Union officially recognizes 88 constellations. In contrast, a comet is an icy body that develops a tail when near the Sun. A meteorite is a space object that reaches Earth's surface, while a meteoroid is a smaller rock or particle in space.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Largest constellation by area? → Hydra
☛ Smallest constellation? → Crux (Southern Cross)
☛ Which constellation contains the Big Dipper? → Ursa Major
☛ Number of officially recognized constellations? → 88
☛ Which constellation contains the Pole Star? → Ursa Minor

question: Which of the following is not a renewable source of energy? (RRB JE EE (19/09/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: Nuclear energy
Hydropower
Biomass
Energy from waste
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nuclear energy

Explanation:
Nuclear energy is not a renewable source because it relies on finite fuels like uranium, which can be depleted. In contrast, hydropower, biomass, and energy from waste are renewable. Hydropower is generated from the water cycle, biomass from organic matter, and energy from waste uses garbage as fuel. Renewable energy sources are naturally replenished and can be used sustainably.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is the main fuel for nuclear energy? → Uranium
☛ Hydropower is the conversion of what energy? → Mechanical energy
☛ What is the main source of biomass? → Plants and organic waste
☛ What is the process of energy from waste called? → Waste-to-energy
☛ What is the biggest advantage of renewable energy? → Unlimited availability
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा ऊर्जा का नवीकरणीय स्रोत नहीं है? (RRB JE EE (19/09/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)

पनबिजली

परमाणु ऊर्जा नवीकरणीय स्रोत नहीं है क्योंकि यह यूरेनियम जैसे सीमित ईंधन पर निर्भर करती है, जो समाप्त हो सकता है। इसके विपरीत, पनबिजली, बायोमास और अपशिष्ट से ऊर्जा नवीकरणीय हैं। पनबिजली जल चक्र से उत्पन्न होती है, बायोमास कार्बनिक पदार्थों से बनता है, और अपशिष्ट से ऊर्जा कचरे को ईंधन के रूप में उपयोग करती है। नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा स्रोत प्राकृतिक रूप से पुनः भर जाते हैं और इनका निरंतर उपयोग संभव है।

question: The ocean covers ________ percentage of Earth’s surface.  (RRB JE EE (19/09/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: 61%
51%
91%
71%
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 71%

Explanation:
Approximately 71% of Earth's surface is covered by oceans, while only 29% is land. Oceans are a major part of Earth's hydrosphere and contain about 97% of Earth's total water. There are five major oceans: the Pacific Ocean (largest), Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern Ocean, and Arctic Ocean. Oceans play a crucial role in regulating Earth's climate, producing oxygen, and hosting immense biodiversity.

☛ What % of Earth's surface is covered by water? → 71%
☛ Which is the largest ocean? → Pacific Ocean
☛ How many oceans are there on Earth? → 5

question: “Ozone Hole” is a - (RRB JE EE (19/09/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: Hole in the atmosphere
Hole in the troposphere
Hole in the thermosphere
Destruction of ozone layer
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Destruction of ozone layer

Explanation:
The term "ozone hole" does not refer to an actual hole in the atmosphere but to the thinning or destruction of the ozone layer. The ozone layer is located in the stratosphere and protects Earth from harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation. This destruction is primarily caused by chemicals like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), which break down ozone molecules. The ozone hole was first discovered over Antarctica in 1985. Its effects include increased cases of skin cancer and cataracts. The Montreal Protocol (1987) banned CFCs, leading to the recovery of the ozone layer.

question: Identify the non-renewable source of energy from the following.  (RRB JE EE (19/09/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)

Coal
Wave power
solution:

Explanation:

Coal is a fossil fuel formed from decomposed plant matter over millions of years and is considered non-renewable because its formation rate is extremely slow. In contrast, fuel cells are devices that convert chemical energy into electricity but are not an energy source themselves. Wind power and wave power are renewable as they are continuously generated by natural processes. Coal is widely used for electricity generation and industrial processes, but burning it releases carbon dioxide and other pollutants. Other non-renewable sources include petroleum, natural gas, and nuclear fuel. The use of non-renewable sources leads to depletion and environmental concerns, making the shift to renewables important.

question: How many prominent stars are present in the Ursa Major constellation, which has the shape of a big dipper?   (RRB JE (29/05/2019) Shift 2 CBT 1)

Six stars

question: From the full moon day counted as day 1, on which day the moon becomes invisible? (RRB JE CBT I (01/06/2019) Shift 2)
options: Thirteenth day
Tenth day
Fifteenth day
Twelfth day
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fifteenth day

Explanation:
Counting the full moon day as day 1, the moon becomes invisible on the 15th day, which is called new moon day (Amavasya). This occurs when the moon comes between the Earth and the Sun, so its illuminated side faces away from Earth. It is the last day of the lunar month. From full moon to new moon, the visible portion of the moon decreases each day. This period is called the waning phase (Krishna Paksha). The moon disappears completely only on Amavasya.

question: Which of the following is the longest river in the Peninsular region of India? (RRB JE CBT I (01/06/2019) Shift 3)
options: Cauvery
Godavari
Mahanadi
Narmada
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Godavari

Explanation:
The longest river in the Peninsular region of India is the Godavari. It is also known as the Dakshin Ganga (Southern Ganges). The Godavari originates from Trimbakeshwar in Nashik district of Maharashtra and has a length of about 1465 km. It flows through the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. Other options: Cauvery (length 800 km), Mahanadi (length 858 km), Narmada (length 1312 km). The Godavari also has the largest drainage basin among Peninsular rivers.
